business_problem: Aura Cloud wanted to strengthen its transaction-monitoring and default-detection capabilities because classification and categorization inside its banking platform were too limited to deliver the insight and automation it wanted for financial-institution clients.
solution_summary: Aura Cloud worked with IBM Client Engineering and the IBM Innovation Studio to test IBM watsonx.ai against the transaction-monitoring workflows inside Aura's digital banking platform. In a four-week pilot, the team evaluated how foundation models could sit behind Aura's existing tools as a back-end insight layer for default detection. The design used watsonx.ai to analyze structured transaction data, improve transaction classification and categorization, and support richer data discovery using text-to-SQL style logic. Rather than replacing Aura's platform, the pilot focused on augmenting it so deviations from standard behavior could be identified faster and summarized more clearly for downstream users. The result was a practical generative-AI architecture for financial-risk workflows that Aura expects to productionize to improve insight generation, simplify analysis, and enhance client experience.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Provides the foundation-model and text-to-SQL capabilities Aura piloted to improve transaction classification, data discovery, and default detection.

data_flow: Structured banking-transaction data from Aura's monitoring tools is passed into watsonx.ai, where foundation-model logic classifies activity, surfaces deviations, and generates richer transaction insights that feed back into Aura's platform.
business_outcome: The pilot gave Aura a credible path to more automated and accurate default-detection workflows, with the company expecting stronger transaction insight generation and better client-facing experiences when the watsonx.ai design is fully implemented.
metrics: more than 80% improvements within transaction insight generation
